programme.title: There's always fear
programme.desc: Steve's crew battles a fiery wreck in the heart of Toronto; the OPP takes to the air to keep the roads safe; when freezing rain ices up the highway around London, a newly-promoted rotator operator gets his first big test.

programme.title: Not the best spot to be
programme.desc: A pileup on the 401 brings traffic to a standstill and pushes the Ross crew into action; Sonny helps a driver stuck on a dangerous stretch of highway in Toronto; Herb's rookie Zach masters a difficult move for the first time.

programme.title: Free the highway
programme.desc: A 70-vehicle whiteout crash shuts down Highway 400 and the OPP jumps to organize an army of recovery crews; the Sarnia team struggles to recover a severely damaged trailer without losing the load.

programme.title: Pull n' pray
programme.desc: Eric is still working to find his place on the new County/Coxon team when a T-bone semi collision spurs them into action; with his first baby on the way, a blizzard in the east sends Andrew on an urgent rescue mission.

programme.title: A big problem
programme.desc: An air ambulance crew takes off after a pileup results in serious casualties; when a low bridge knocks over an industrial payload, Steve and crew battle their way through a sandstorm.

programme.title: Holy Mackerel, what a mess
programme.desc: After a triple crash, the crew from Chatham struggles to keep a mangled truck in one piece; a complicated air cushion job tests a new rotator operator; the new heavy crew at Metro gets a bad case of déjà vu.

programme.title: That Highway is the Lifeline
programme.desc: Herb's team fights fire while tussling with a burned-out semi; as whiteouts rage across the 402 in Sarnia, Mark fights his way through a long backup to reach a job; a unique recovery crew faces a heavy load of peat moss and trailer ready to split.

programme.title: A Real Disaster
programme.desc: With his dad away, Mitch works with his older brother to get a stubborn wreck onto the road, but these brothers rarely see eye-to-eye; Glen, Todd and the crew improvise to offload some extreme cargo.

programme.title: I've seen my share
programme.desc: When a rolled-over dump truck spills its load on the 401 in the middle of rush hour, Steve, Sonny and crew must make a split-second decision; Eric and his boss disagree on how to handle a shredded trailer.

programme.title: You are never safe
programme.desc: Snow squalls attack Highway 402, sending Gary, Collin and Mark to work deep in the trees; a fuel tanker rolls next to rail lines in Toronto's industrial port lands; the Chatham crew improvises against a fire-ravaged wreck.

programme.title: Always makes my knee knock
programme.desc: Mitch's new partnership with his brother is put to the test in the aftermath of a brutal storm; Eric, Derek and crew take on a load of steel pipes threatening to spring loose on the road; Andrew and his team wrestle difficult cargo.

programme.title: It's a rush every time
programme.desc: Gary's crew and family come together for a multi-wreck scene blocking the border; low power lines and a bad fuel leak complicate a delicate recovery in Toronto; a garbage hauler creates a heavy mess for the Ross crew.

programme.title: Big, Mean and Heavy
programme.desc: A load of lumber spills across the 401 in the heart of Toronto, John Allen heads into the first storm of the season; after an injury on the job, Gary must lean on Collin for a heavy yet delicate recovery; Sonny makes a major change in his life.

programme.title: The worst place
programme.desc: The OPP must manage a chaotic scene after a thirty-vehicle pileup shuts down the 401; Mitch sets a tight deadline in his first job as leader of the heavy crew; a semi smashes into a culvert, the Ross's try out their newest operator.

programme.title: Everything that can go wrong
programme.desc: Sonny and his new boss face their first heavy test, fighting a semi frozen hard into the mud; a double collision brings border traffic to a halt in Sarnia, forcing Gary and crew to wrangle a difficult load of cargo.

programme.title: A Hell of a Pull
programme.desc: A rolled-over load of scrap metal defies gravity and Kevin's patience; the Cornwall crew rides to the rescue of a fire truck; County Towing struggles to get a grip on an icy highway.

programme.title: Orlando Finals
programme.desc: Thirty competitors face obstacles that include Salmon Ladder, Cannonball Alley, Helix Hang and Invisible Ladder on the Orlando finals course.

programme.title: Pittsburgh Finals
programme.desc: Competitors in the Pittsburgh finals face obstacles that include Salmon Ladder, Floating Monkey Bars, Door Knob Arch and Invisible Ladder.

programme.title: Military Finals
programme.desc: Thirty competitors face obstacles that include Salmon Ladder, Arm Rings, Doorknob Arch and Spider Climb.

programme.title: Best Runs of 2015
programme.desc: A jam-packed review includes the best moments of the season so far.

programme.title: Vegas Finals
programme.desc: The top finishers from the regional finals face a course modeled after Mount Midoriyama in Japan; obstacles include the Sonic Curve and the Double Shock.

programme.title: Vegas Finals
programme.desc: The top finishers from the regional finals face a course modeled after Mount Midoriyama in Japan; obstacles include the Sonic Curve and the Double Shock.

programme.title: Vegas Finals
programme.desc: In the last night of the Las Vegas finals, competitors tackle obstacles that include Psycho Chain and Area 51.

programme.title: All Stars Special
programme.desc: The hosts pick some of the fastest, strongest and most impressive athletes from the show to compete against each other on the national finals course.

programme.title: Los Angeles Qualifier
programme.desc: Contestants gear up for the qualifying round of the extreme obstacle course competition; floating steps, tic toc, escalator and ring jump are among the new obstacles for Season 8.

programme.title: Atlanta Qualifier
programme.desc: In Atlanta, competitors are challenged with six obstacles, including Floating Steps, Block Run and Pipe Fitter.

programme.title: Indianapolis Qualifier
programme.desc: Competitors in Indianapolis take on six obstacles, including Floating Steps, Fly Wheels and Disk Runner; racecar drivers Ricky Stenhouse Jr., Josef Newgarden, Tony Kanaan and Hélio Castroneves.

programme.title: Oklahoma City Qualifier
programme.desc: Competitors in Oklahoma City take on obstacles, including Floating Steps, Ring Swing and Rock 'n' Roll.

programme.title: Philadelphia Qualifier
programme.desc: Competitors in Philadelphia take on obstacles, including Wall Drop and Rolling Thunder.

programme.title: Los Angeles Finals
programme.desc: Competitors from the Los Angeles qualifier travel back to Universal Studios to conquer the City Finals course as well as compete on the Salmon Ladder, The Wedge, and the Helix Hang.

programme.title: Los Angeles Finals
programme.desc: Competitors from the Los Angeles qualifier travel back to Universal Studios to conquer the City Finals course as well as compete on the Salmon Ladder, The Wedge, and the Helix Hang.

programme.title: Indianapolis Finals
programme.desc: The top 30 competitors from the city qualifier take on even more demanding obstacles, including the Salmon Ladder, the Hourglass Drop and the Circuit Board, as they fight for a place at the Las Vegas finals.

programme.title: Oklahoma City Finals
programme.desc: The top 30 competitors from the city qualifier take on more challenges, including the Salmon Ladder, Bungee Road, Pinch Grab and Invisible Ladder.

programme.title: Philadelphia Finals
programme.desc: The top 30 competitors take on a more challenging course that has 10 obstacles, including the Salmon Ladder and Flying Shelf Grab.

programme.title: National Finals Week 1
programme.desc: The top competitors from the city finals face a four-stage course with new obstacles, including the Snake Run, Giant Log Grip, Broken Bridge, and Flying Squirrel.

programme.title: National Finals Week 2
programme.desc: The remaining competitors take on the four-stage course, including the Snake Run, Giant Log Grip, Broken Bridge and Flying Squirrel.

programme.title: National Finals Week 3
programme.desc: The top competitors from the city finals face the last three stages of Mount Midoriyama, with five new obstacles, including the Giant Ring Swing, the Hourglass to Atari and the Double Wedge.

programme.title: All Stars
programme.desc: Hosts Matt and Akbar select teams consisting of three competitors to compete for the championship trophy in super-sized skills and obstacles competitions.

programme.title: USA vs. the World
programme.desc: Teams from North America, Latin America and Europe travel to Las Vegas, where they tackle the punishing finals course; competitors include Brian Arnold, Drew Drechsel, Daniel Gil, Jessie Graff, Josh Levin and Jake Murray.

programme.title: Los Angeles Qualifiers
programme.desc: In the first qualifying round from Los Angeles, competitors must tackle six obstacles, including Cannonball Drop and Battering Ram; American Ninja Warrior veterans Kevin Bull and Grant McCartney return for another shot at completing the course.

programme.title: San Antonio Qualifiers
programme.desc: Indy car driver Conor Daly and Olympic gold medalist Jonathan Horton are among the competitors in San Antonio who tackle two new obstacles: the Spinning Bridge and Skyhooks.

programme.title: Daytona Beach Qualifiers
programme.desc: Competitors tackle six obstacles, including the brand new Rolling Pin and Wing nuts; veteran "American Ninja Warrior" fan favorites Jessie Graff, Drew Drechsel, and JJ Woods return; NASCAR driver Ben Kennedy takes on the course for the first time.

programme.title: Kansas City Qualifiers
programme.desc: Competitors face six challenging obstacles, including the Hang Glider, Broken Pipes and Crank It Up; veterans Lance Pekus, Brandon Mears and Dan Polizzi return; Olympic decathlete Jeremy Taiwo takes on the course.

programme.title: Cleveland Qualifiers
programme.desc: Competitors tackle Razor's Edge and I-Beam Gap; returning players include the "fantastic four" from last season: Alyssa Beird, Rachel Goldstein, Jesse "Flex" Labreck and Michelle Warnky.

programme.title: Denver Qualifiers
programme.desc: Competitors face three new obstacles called Bouncing Spider, Rail Runner and Ninjago Roll.

programme.title: Los Angeles City Finals
programme.desc: The top 30 competitors from the Los Angeles qualifier tackle obstacles, including the Salmon Ladder, Stair Hopper, Swinging Peg Board and Elevator Climb.

programme.title: Final Main
programme.desc: It is main course day and with only two spots remaining on the banquet menu, the competition is fierce. As the barbecues are fired up, all eight chefs are feeling the heat. The judges are joined by guest judge Gordon Reid.

programme.title: Final Dessert
programme.desc: It is dessert day and with just one place remaining at the Wimbledon banquet, each chef is giving everything they have got. The judges are joined by guest judge Annabel Croft, former British number one and Junior Wimbledon champion.

programme.title: Banquet
programme.desc: It's the grand finale and the winning chefs must now cook their dishes at the banquet. Once in the kitchen, the chefs face the huge challenge of scaling up their dishes.

programme.title: North East Starter
programme.desc: Competing for top spot are Danny Parker, head chef at Michelin starred 'House of Tides' in Newcastle, who is back to try his luck in the competition again after being knocked out in the regional heat last year following a tense tie-break. He's taking on two newcomers: Dan Fletcher, protégé of Phil Howard, and now head chef at 'Fenchurch' in the City of London, and David Coulson, who runs 'Peace and Loaf' in Newcastle, which boasts 2 AA rosettes.

programme.title: North East Fish
programme.desc: After a tense starter course the chefs are all aiming for 10s with their unique fish dishes. David is celebrating a personal connection to the brief with his `My Cod I Bet Me Ma'am Has Seen Some Trotters', a tribute to his mum who has worked as a chiropodist. Dan's `For All Those Sleepless Nights' pays tribute to night shift workers from the NHS with some bold but classic flavours while Danny's `Not All Superheroes Wear Capes' aims to give a taste of luxury to the hardworking staff.

programme.title: North East Main
programme.desc: Dan pays tribute to an icon of modern nursing, Florence Nightingale, while Danny is inspired by the founder of the NHS, Aneurin Bevan. David's dish is dedicated to the air ambulance staff who saved the life of his fiancé, and he even takes a trip to meet one of them.

programme.title: North East Dessert
programme.desc: It's the chefs' last chance to impress and tensions are high. Dan takes a risk with an unusual combination of ewe's milk and bergamot while Danny is determined to pull out all the stops with his complex dessert `Aunty Gwen's Chocolate'. David hopes to transform a childhood comfort classic into a show stopping dessert. Dan also takes a trip to meet Dr Ben Clarke who was working in the Royal London Hospital A&E during the London Bridge terror attack.

programme.title: North East Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining North East chefs must cook their four-course menus again, but will they take on board their veteran's advice as they serve their 'Feast To Say Thank You'?

programme.title: London South East Starter
programme.desc: Banquet champion Selin Kiazim, a rising star of the London scene renowned for her Turkish Cypriot fusion flavours, is back hoping to join the elite group of chefs who have made it to the banquet twice. She is up against James Cochran who's worked at some of London's toughest kitchens including 2 Michelin starred 'The Ledbury' and Scott Goss from 'The Twenty Six' in Tunbridge Wells, renowned for his use of local Kent ingredients.

programme.title: London South East Fish
programme.desc: The chefs do battle for the fish course and the atmosphere in the kitchen is tense. Lobster is catch of the day for James whose dish is Caribbean-inspired. Scott is attempting to elevate a classic fish pie, dedicated to his mum who worked as a pharmacist in the NHS for 23 years. And Selin is taking a risk with a complex three-part fish dish featuring sardines, scallops and langoustines, as a nod to the purported health benefits of a Mediterranean diet.

programme.title: London South East Main
programme.desc: Scott is showcasing rare-breed Tamworth pork to say thank you to the rare breed of people who work for the NHS. Selin is serving a complex duck dish using ingredients from all around the world to honour `Our Global NHS'. And James is presenting five cuts of goat cooked in five different ways, for his bold dish `Under The Knife'.

programme.title: London South East Dessert
programme.desc: Selin puts her own unique twist on tea and toast. James creates a decadent coconut parfait accompanied by mango purée filled doughnuts for his dessert 'Tree of Life' inspired by the coconut palm tree, the NHS and both of their contributions to our health. Scott hopes his elevated gypsy tart 'Honey Bee Good' will secure him a place in the final.

programme.title: London South East Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining London and the south-east chefs must cook their four-course menus again, but will they take on board their veteran's advice as they remake their 'Feast To Say Thank You'?

programme.title: Scotland Starter
programme.desc: Vying to be crowned champion of Scotland are three newcomers to the GBM kitchen. Lorna McNee is a former Scottish Chef of the Year and is renowned for her technical precision, gained from working at two-Michelin-starred restaurant 'Andrew Fairlie'.

programme.title: Scotland Fish
programme.desc: It is the fish course and the chefs are all out to impress. The heat is increased as all three serve their unique takes on lobster. Ross seeks victory with his dish 'Lobster Aid'. Lorna's 'Live Well, Live Very Well' features only three elements.

programme.title: Scotland Main
programme.desc: Ross is hoping to impress with 'Oh Deer It's Time For Your Penicillin', his tribute to Scottish scientist Alexander Fleming featuring an unusual yeast element as well as venison. Across the kitchen, Lorna, a former Game Chef of the Year, is also cooking venison in a bid to impress.

programme.title: Scotland Dessert
programme.desc: Ross is attempting to elevate a classic into a dish worthy of the banquet, Lorna is cooking a personal tribute to NHS staff using unusual yuzu and tonka bean flavours, and Ben is serving an experimental dish which includes a beeswax ice cream.

programme.title: Scotland Judging
programme.desc: It is judging day and the two remaining chefs must impress the panel of Oliver Peyton, Andi Oliver and Matthew Fort. Both chefs are gunning for success and are doing everything they can to deliver their menus to perfection.

programme.title: Central Starter
programme.desc: Three chefs compete in the heat for the central region. Returner Ryan Simson-Trotman, who failed to reach the national finals last year, is originally from Nuneaton and opened his own restaurant Orwells in the Oxfordshire countryside with his partner Liam, who is also a contestant in the North West region.

programme.title: Central Fish
programme.desc: It is the fish course and the chefs are pulling out all the stops. Marianne pays tribute to the `angels' in her local hospital who looked after her during a recent illness, and Ryan's dish is a reference to the purported health benefits of fish high in omega 3 oils, while Sabrina is inspired by her aunt, a retired nurse who used to take in food to share with her fellow workers during her shifts.

programme.title: Central Main
programme.desc: The chefs cook their mains and, following the previous day's results, tension is high. Both Marianne and Ryan are cooking muntjac in the hope of impressing the veteran judge, while Sabrina is making an ambitious technical take on a family feast.

programme.title: Central Dessert
programme.desc: With one dish left to impress the veteran judge, the chefs cook their desserts. Marianne is looking to raise a smile with her 'carry on' themed dessert, complete with surprise presentation. Sabrina hopes to make it through with an elevated take on jelly and ice cream while Ryan goes all out with his very sweet treat 'A Spoonful of Sugar'.

programme.title: Central Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining central region chefs do battle for a place in the national finals. They must impress the formidable panel of Andi Oliver, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton with their four-course menus.

programme.title: Wales Starter
programme.desc: Andrew is attempting to pay tribute to NHS staff with his take on a traditional healing recipe, 'Mum's Flu-Fighting Chicken Soup'. Jason's 'A Tea From The Heart' is a play on a post-war remedy which harks back to the era when the NHS was formed.

programme.title: Wales Fish
programme.desc: After the starter results, the chefs return to the kitchen hoping for high scores with their fish dishes. Chris once again is using ingredients he has foraged from around his restaurant, while Jason hopes to impress with a spicy scallop dish and Andrew prepares a cod dish with 11 different elements.

programme.title: Wales Main
programme.desc: The chefs are pulling out all the stops in a bid for big scores with their mains. All three dishes pay tribute to the founder of the NHS Aneurin Bevan, Chris's 'Everything But The Squeal' is an ambitious pork sharing platter, while Jason's 'For The Rich And The Poor' showcases lamb, and Andrew is hoping to impress with 'Aneurin Bevan For Better Steak'.

programme.title: Wales Dessert
programme.desc: It is the dessert course and the last opportunity for the chefs to impress. Chris is hoping to triumph with another dish which showcases the foraged ingredients available around his restaurant, while Jason attempts a technical feat in his dessert inspired by a childhood hospital stay and Andrew is inspired by a dish by his great-grandmother used to cook. Which two will make it through to the judging chamber?

programme.title: Wales Judging
programme.desc: It is the Wales regional final as the two remaining chefs do everything they can to impress the judging panel of Andi Oliver, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton. After tensions ran high in the week, the chefs are under pressure to deliver perfection. The judges are joined by Aneira Thomas, the first baby born on the NHS, who is named in tribute to the service's founder Aneurin Bevan and who went on to dedicate her life to the service. Who will win a place in the national finals?

programme.title: South West Starter
programme.desc: It's the turn of three chefs representing the south-west, including two who have competed before but meet in the kitchen this week for the very first time. The chefs meet their surprise veteran judge and cook their celebratory starters.

programme.title: South West Fish
programme.desc: It's the fish course and with Tom renowned as a fish specialist all eyes are on him. He's cooking his take on a classic British fish supper in tribute to a charity which looks after the health of local fishermen. Jude is attempting a complex fusion dish featuring four different fish and an unusual X-Ray themed presentation, while Olivia is paying tribute to the staff who looked after her during the birth of her first son with her take on curried monkfish.

programme.title: South West Main
programme.desc: It's the main course and two of the chefs are hoping duck will win the day. Tom is preparing a technically challenging duck dish steeped in NHS history while Jude is making a multi-element Chinese duck dish inspired by his mum. Olivia is hoping her dish, using two unusual cuts of beef, will score top points. Olivia also visits her local children's hospital, home of the second-busiest paediatric A&E in the country.

programme.title: South West Dessert
programme.desc: With just one more chance to impress their veteran judge, the chefs are all hoping to use their pastry skills to deliver technically complex desserts. Tom's cooking an 'Invalid Fruit Tart' inspired by a 1950s recipe, while Jude is making six different apple elements for his 'An Apple A Day'. Olivia is using stout in reference to an outdated old wives' tale which suggested the drink was a healthy source of iron during pregnancy.

programme.title: South West Judging
programme.desc: It's time for the two remaining chefs representing the South West to go head-to-head as they cook their menus again for the exacting panel of Andi Oliver, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton. With a spot in the National Finals at stake, both are aiming for perfection as they bid for glory. The judges are joined by Barbara Childs, a Matron in the Cardiac Intensive Care Unit at Great Ormond Street Hospital, who isn't afraid to speak her mind in the chamber.

programme.title: North West Starter
programme.desc: Three chefs take to the kitchen in a bid to represent the north-west in the national final. They include Ellis Barrie, from the award-winning Marram Grass in Anglesey, Liam Simpson-Trotman, an accomplished pastry chef and co-owner of the 4 AA rosette Orwell's in Oxfordshire, and Craig Sherrington, who sharpened his skills working under top names including Eric Chavot and is now Chef Patron of Virginia House in Cumbria.

programme.title: North West Fish
programme.desc: It's the fish course and the chefs are all gunning for tens. Craig pays tribute to a friend who has revolutionised hospital food in Morecambe Bay, while Liam is inspired by health advice his grandma gave him and Ellis is dedicating his dish to the staff who delivered his son Albert. With cod, mackerel, shrimp and cockles on the menu, which of the chefs will score highly?

programme.title: North West Main
programme.desc: Time for the chefs to cook their mains and the pressure is on. Craig is hoping to impress using two cuts of Dexter beef, while Liam prepares his take on a Bajan lamb stew and Ellis prepares four cuts of suckling pig. Liam meets his personal hero, Nola Ishmael OBE, who became the UK's first ever black Director of Nursing.

programme.title: North West Dessert
programme.desc: It's the dessert course and the last chance for the North West chefs to impress in a bid to make it through to the regional final. Liam is cooking 'Not So Hot Toddy' in honour of a friend who works night shifts in the NHS, while Ellis' 'Worth Their Weight in Gold' is dedicated to the staff who saved his brother's life and Craig's dish 'The Missed Celebration' pays tribute to his wife with an unusual Christmas concept.

programme.title: North West Judging
programme.desc: The two highest scoring chefs from the week return to cook their menus again. Judging them are Matthew Fort, Oliver Peyton and Andi Oliver who are joined by Dr Jake Dunning MBE, an infectious disease specialist who has been recognised for his work during the West Africa Ebola epidemic.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Starter
programme.desc: Three chefs are doing battle to represent Northern Ireland. Tommy Heaney, Head Chef at the Great House Hotel in South Wales, is taken on by Shauna Froydenlund, Chef Patron at Marcus Wareing's two Michelin starred restaurant, and James Devine, the 2017 National Chef of the Year.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Fish
programme.desc: After a tense starter course, the chefs return to the kitchen to cook their fish dishes. James is making his elevated take on a fried chicken takeaway as a tribute to the NHS staff who care for his sister. Shauna is also taking inspiration from a personal connection with a tribute to staff from a facility in her hometown of Londonderry. Tommy is hoping to impress with a dish dedicated to the discovery of DNA.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Main
programme.desc: With two courses down it's time for the chefs to cook their main courses. It's the battle of beef with each using the same meat in their innovative creations. Tommy also meets the first baby ever born on the NHS.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Dessert
programme.desc: It's the dessert course and the final chance for the chefs to impress. After such a tightly fought battle all week, each is hoping to deliver a technically perfect dessert. Tommy and James are both using passion fruit in their complex dishes while Shauna is hoping to use her pastry chef training to score full marks.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Judging
programme.desc: The two chefs representing Northern Ireland go head-to-head. Judging as ever are Oliver Peyton, Matthew Fort and Andi Oliver who are joined by Shehan Hettiaratchy, lead trauma surgeon at St Mary's Hospital who helped treat victims of the Grenfell Tower fire.

programme.title: Finals Starter
programme.desc: The winning chefs from all eight regions must battle it out for the honour of a spot on 2018's 'Feast To Say Thank You' banquet menu, celebrating 70 years of the NHS, one of Britain's most prized institutions.

programme.title: Finals Fish
programme.desc: The chefs must prepare fish courses, and after some exceptionally high-scoring dishes in the starter round, everyone is desperate to deliver perfection. Once again, the chefs present their innovative, witty and heart-warming creations.

programme.title: Finals Main
programme.desc: It's main course day and with only two spots remaining on the banquet menu, the competition is fierce. Both chefs and judges alike are amazed at the high standard of cooking and an incredible number of 10s are dished out as the chefs serve up venison, rabbit, duck, beef, lamb and pork for scrutiny.

programme.title: Finals Dessert
programme.desc: It's dessert day and with just one place remaining at the banquet feast, each chef is giving everything they've got for a chance to say thank you to the heroic NHS staff. All the chefs have significantly re-worked or re-invented their desserts since the regional heats, proving that they'll do everything they can in a bid for that final winning spot.

programme.title: Banquet
programme.desc: It's the grand finale as the winning chefs cook their dishes at a banquet for the heroes of the NHS. Having arrived at St Bartholomew's Hospital, the chefs are shown the incredible location for event, the almost three-hundred-year-old Great Hall.

programme.title: London and South East - Starter and Fish Courses
programme.desc: Competing for the top spot are 3 new chefs to the competition representing some of the most exciting culinary talent from London, Paul Walsh, Luke Selby and Ben Marks.

programme.title: London and South East Mains and Desserts
programme.desc: The three chefs are halfway through their heat and the pressure is mounting. Only two will proceed to Friday's judging and have a chance to represent the London and the South East region at the regional finals.

programme.title: London and South East - Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining London chefs must cook their four-course menus again. The chefs need to impress the formidable judges: food writer Matthew Fort, restaurateur Oliver Peyton and broadcaster and cook Andi Oliver as well as a guest judge.

programme.title: North East: Starter and Fish Courses
programme.desc: Three chefs new to the competition compete in the North East heats. Three of the region's chefs battle it out for the top spot: Mike Carr, Samira Effa, and Tom Anglesea. The three chefs must present the menu of their careers, inspired by 50 years of British pop music.

programme.title: North East: Main and Dessert
programme.desc: The chefs are halfway through their heat and will serve up their main courses and desserts. The stakes are high, and again they are each serving a unique take on the pop music brief. Mike is confident about his northern dish, 'Rack n Roll', which puts both classic Yorkshire hogget and traditional Lancashire hotpot in the spotlight.

programme.title: North East: Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining North East chefs must cook their four-course menus again for the judges: food writer Matthew Fort, restaurateur Oliver Peyton and broadcaster and cook Andi Oliver as well as a guest judge, one of the British pop industry's finest.

programme.title: Central Starter and Fish Courses
programme.desc: Newcomer Kray brings an urban edge to proceedings, with a starter inspired by grime music called 'Fire in the Booth'. It combines hot sauce, veal sweetbreads and tuna belly. Returner Sabrina is compiling a dish of her favourite ingredients, including pasta and ox cheek, for her Italian inspired starter called 'My Mixtape'.

programme.title: Central Main and Dessert
programme.desc: For his main course, Ryan Simpson-Trotman is confident his dish, `The UK's Number 1', will hit the top spot with his combination of a beef pie and rump cap. Sabrina Gidda is taking inspiration from her grandad's collection of old 45s for her `Sunday Jukebox' main: pork Wellington and Black Country faggots.

programme.title: Central Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining Central chefs must cook their four-course menus again for judges food writer Matthew Fort, restaurateur Oliver Peyton and broadcaster and cook Andi Oliver as well as a guest judge.

programme.title: North West Starter and Fish
programme.desc: Competing for a place on the banquet menu are two chefs returning to the competition for a second time, plus a supremely talented newcomer. Liam Simpson, who co-owns a high-end gastropub near Henley-on-Thames, is hoping to make it all the way after being knocked out in the heats during the 2018 competition.

programme.title: North West Main and Dessert
programme.desc: The chefs are halfway through the regional heats and, as the lowest scoring chef will be eliminated from the competition at the end of the show, the pressure is on. They start by cooking their all-important main courses, the centrepiece of the banquet menu. Michelin-starred newcomer Hrishikesh Desai is pushing himself to the limit with a complex multipart venison dish, inspired by the bands which play at the Kendal Calling music festival.

programme.title: North West Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining chefs from the north-west cook their dishes head to head for a panel of expert judges, in a bid to secure themselves a place in the national finals. Will they have acted on the advice given by the veteran judge earlier in the week, and learn from their mistakes?

programme.title: Scotland Starter and Fish Courses
programme.desc: Three of Scotland's finest chefs do battle for a chance to cook at the banquet celebrating 50 Years of Popular Music. Gordon Jones, the only newcomer, faces returners Lorna McNee and Ben Reade, who are going head-to-head for the second time.

programme.title: Scotland Main and Dessert
programme.desc: The chefs cook their mains and desserts, each battling to produce smash hit dishes that wow their veteran. For her main, Lorna is confident her lamb dish `With A Little Help From My Friends', dedicated to supportive friends, is a celebratory dish fit for the banquet.

programme.title: Scotland Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining Scottish chefs must cook their four courses again, but this time they'll need to appeal to four new palates. Food writer Matthew Fort, restaurateur Oliver Peyton, broadcaster and cook Andi Oliver plus a celebrity guest judge.

programme.title: South West Starter and Fish
programme.desc: Emily Scott is the chef proprietor of Cornwall's renowned 'St Tudy Inn'. Her two rivals are from across the sea on Jersey. Joe Baker is largely self-taught, but at just 28 already running his own restaurant, 'No 10', in St Helier. A neighbouring restaurant is Michelin starred 'Samphire' where Lee Smith is head chef.

programme.title: South West Mains and Dessert
programme.desc: Emily's David Bowie-inspired dish celebrates Britain's food heroes, and she uses Cornish duck meat from her local producer that she pairs with grilled radicchio and Malbec sauce. Meanwhile, Joe has also sourced his ingredients locally.

programme.title: South West Judging
programme.desc: The chefs need to impress the esteemed judges: food writer Matthew Fort, restaurateur Oliver Peyton and broadcaster and cook Andi Oliver as well as a guest judge, one of the pop stars the banquet will celebrate. They are joined by one half of the synthpop duo The Communards, Reverend Richard Coles.

programme.title: La tribu
programme.desc: Tertulia de referencia del panorama futbolístico. Un espacio en el que la actualidad, el análisis y el debate se combinan con opiniones de primer nivel para ofrecer una visión completa del fútbol.

programme.title: La pizarra de Quintana
programme.desc: Espacio de referencia del panorama futbolístico dedicado al análisis, la actualidad y el debate que acompaña cada día a los aficionados al fútbol.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty prepares for late spring and summer, while Toby Buckland revels in some spring planting at Melbourne Hall in Derbyshire. Rachel de Thame meets a dahlia grower who once worked at the White House.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Frances Tophill reveals some exciting news. After years of dreaming, she finally has her very own garden and can't wait to share her plans and get to grips with bringing this compact space to life.

programme.title: Central Spain
programme.desc: Monty travels across Central Spain. He begins at the vast, imposing palace and garden of the Escorial before heading for Madrid, Toledo, other parts of Castile and finally Valencia.

programme.title: Southern Spain
programme.desc: Monty Don is in the south of Spain, visiting gardens that show how this part of the country has evolved thanks to influences from visitors and settlers from ancient to modern times.

programme.title: Northern Spain
programme.desc: Monty Don travels across northern Spain, visiting gardens across this vast and diverse landscape that changes from an Atlantic to a Mediterranean climate as he journeys from Galicia to Catalonia.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: With autumn on the horizon, the seasonal planting of bulbs for spring-flowering begins at Longmeadow. Frances Tophill meets a gardener whose allotment is filled with both traditional and exotic vegetables and Toby Buckland visits The Newt in Somerset to find out about its chequered garden history and to explore its emergence as one of the UK's most exciting gardens.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: As the plants in the jewel garden reach the peak of their late summer glory, Monty starts planning for the spring when he plants ferns and gives advice on the care and maintenance of wildlife ponds.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: As autumn gathers momentum, it's time to start putting the garden to bed for winter. Monty Don has some timely advice on what to do. Carol Klein meets a nurseryman in Herefordshire, and together they indulge in the beauty of the Japanese maple.

programme.title: Brighton/High Wycombe
programme.desc: In Brighton determined duo Helen and Dax have their hands full with twins, one of whom has special needs. Meanwhile in High Wycombe, newly single Valerie is looking for a fresh lease of life.

programme.title: Bury & Hackney
programme.desc: Monty Don visits two sets of ambitious gardeners, each facing challenges on a very different scale. One is a tiny urban courtyard in Hackney and the other is an outdoor area for a community.

programme.title: Essex & Ipswich
programme.desc: Monty meets two sets of gardeners who have unimaginable ambitions for their outdoor spaces. In Essex Denise has never ventured beyond the decking area behind her house. Meanwhile in Ipswich, a father and daughter plan to build a terraced allotment.

programme.title: Leicester
programme.desc: In Leicester the team meet Paul, a personal trainer who would like to use his space for clients, as well as for relaxing with friends and family. Can the team give him an all-purpose garden that also takes into consideration his disability?

programme.title: Bourne
programme.desc: Charlie Dimmock and the Rich Brothers are tasked with bringing a tropical vibe to a sparse garden in Lincolnshire. Lizzie and Mike want the colours and feel of an island getaway, so which design will they choose?

programme.title: Liphook
programme.desc: The team is in Liphook with a challenge on their hands. Anne and Shaun have a big garden, and a daughter who has her own ideas on what makes a perfect outdoor space. Can the Rich brothers save the day, or will Charlie's design suit the family best?

programme.title: Newport
programme.desc: Tracey and Rob's Newport home has it all: dangerous sloped banks, a multi-level space full of wild weeds, overgrown hedges and too many trees. For those brave enough to make it to the top, however, the garden offers a magnificent view.

programme.title: North Walsham
programme.desc: Charlie and the brothers go head to head to win the right to make over the garden of Christine and Tony, who were shot in a terrorist attack in Tunisia in June 2015. If ever a couple needed the peace and consoling virtues of a garden, it is this one.

programme.title: Monty Don's Japanese Gardens
programme.desc: Monty continues his travels to learn about the art of Japanese stonemasonry and the famous tea ceremonies and their accompanying gardens, before finally taking a lesson in the delicate art of traditional flower arranging.

programme.title: Monty Don's Japanese Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don returns to Japan during the fiery blaze of autumn. He visits the three great gardens of Japan to learn how they protect the garden from the coming winter and learns how the Japanese are weaving nature into their concrete urban jungle.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty is busy planting umbellifers and making some changes to the dry garden. He also sows peas and pots on his dahlias. Carol reveals exciting plans for an ambitious show garden she's designing for the RHS Hampton Court Palace Garden Festival.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Adam visits a walled garden in Somerset to meet a group of volunteers who are gardening alongside those who need help to transform their lives. At Longmeadow, Monty creates two different planting schemes for pots for shady spaces, transplants grasses in the jewel garden, and plants out his favourite varieties of tomatoes.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: A special programme from the first big flower show of the season, the RHS Malvern Spring Festival. Rachel de Thame and Nick Bailey explore show gardens packed full of ideas and discover the newest varieties of plants and flowers that are hot off the potting bench. There are the herb specialists from Gloucestershire who believe that edibles are just as important as ornamentals in the garden, and a nursery famed for its foxgloves that also has an impressive collection of tree peonies.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty is busy planting out tropical gingers and sweetcorn and direct sowing beans. Joe Swift visits a stunning walled garden in Denbighshire, and Rekha Mistry shares the secrets of growing aubergines.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty creates colourful planting schemes with trailing plants. He also plants out cabbages in the vegetable garden and shares a clever tip for dealing with spent tulips. Toby Buckland revels in the displays of roses at Mount Ephraim Gardens in Kent.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Featuring Ramona Jones, who was diagnosed with autism in her twenties and discovered how she can find her true identity when she's in the garden. Meanwhile, Monty makes some changes to his pots in the Jewel Garden, harvests gooseberries and plants out squash.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: The team are Birmingham-bound for the annual Gardeners' World Live event. Monty Don, Arit Anderson, Adam Frost, Sue Kent, Carol Klein, Joe Swift, Rachel de Thame and Frances Tophill present the best the gardening world has to offer.

programme.title: Gardens of Power and Passion
programme.desc: Monty Don visits some of the most famous and interesting gardens in France. Here, he tells the stories behind France's important historic gardens. These include elaborate walled gardens designed to please the mistress - and then the wife - of a King, and magnificent displays of flowers and fountains that involved thousands of soldiers moving tracts of land and incited violent jealousy in another monarch.

programme.title: The Gourmet Garden
programme.desc: Monty Don turns to the French love of food and finds out how this has influenced their gardens. He travels to some of the most famous 'potager' or kitchen gardens, where vegetables and flowers are planted together in elaborate and beautiful displays. He also talks to gardeners about this style of planting which has been copied the world over.

programme.title: The Artistic Garden
programme.desc: Monty Don travels to some of the most celebrated artists' gardens, including the one created by the impressionist Claude Monet, who planted and painted his garden for half his life. Monty also matches the paintings to the garden of Paul Cezanne, as well as visiting several contemporary artistic gardens to see how the use of plants and trees has evolved into new and varied styles.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: At Longmeadow Monty checks the progress of the potatoes he planted earlier in the year and recommends plants for dry shade under trees. We travel to Somerset to get water-saving tips from a water scientist who uses a variety of techniques to save as much water as possible in her own garden, and we meet a gardener who has filled his home with over one thousand houseplants.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Adam Frost shares the progress that's been made in his garden. Frances Tophill heads to the beach to reveal what gardeners can learn from the coastal plants which have evolved to cope with more extreme conditions.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: The team celebrate the bounty our gardens have to offer at this time of year as Carol Klein gathers wild blackberries, Monty Don is at Longmeadow, and we join a champion vegetable grower in Yorkshire as he prepares for the biggest show of the season.

programme.title: Stockport & Tufnell Park
programme.desc: Monty comes to the rescue of two couples in need of help transforming their rubble filled back gardens into havens of peace and tranquillity. They are in serious need of help and advice, but can Monty set them on the right track?

programme.title: Blackpool/Cumbria
programme.desc: Two gardeners, each living on their own, are hoping Monty can help them. In Blackpool, Alex dreams of turning her boring backyard into a magical enchanted forest. Also in Bristol, Ross has taken on a very over-grown allotment.

programme.title: Leyton
programme.desc: In Leyton, Tariq and Sairah want to turn their dumping ground of a backyard into a sumptuous award-winning garden, suitable for entertaining friends and family. Both have competitive jobs in the banking sector and are used to winning at work but when it comes to gardening, they don't know where to begin.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: With summertime at its peak, Adam plans to extend the season with plants for evening scent and shares the results of his wild meadow turf experiment. In North Yorkshire, Nick Bailey discovers the range of floral beauty of Cornus kousa.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty gives a masterclass on rambling, climbing and shrub roses. He also plants out tender annuals in the jewel garden, and with hot, dry summer days ahead, shares tips for water saving and harvesting.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: The show comes from the RHS Hampton Court Palace Garden Festival. Arit Anderson, Toby Buckland and Adam Frost reveal the latest in floral fashions and share highlights of the show gardens and floral marquee.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Coming from the biggest horticultural event in the North, the RHS Flower Show Tatton Park. Joe Swift and Frances Tophill reveal the latest in garden design, as well as bringing plant perfection from some of the best nurseries in the country.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty harvests his spuds and sows seeds for autumn veg. He also shows how to get plants for free by taking cuttings.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: A celebration of people who are growing their own, from vegetables to flowers, across the UK. At Longmeadow, Monty shares tips and advice on how to get the most out of bargain plants. Meanwhile, Joe visits an extraordinary food project in Bristol.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Frances Tophill is in her very first garden for a summer catch-up and an update on her progress since moving in. Meanwhile, Adam Frost meets a kindred spirit who explains how gardening saved his life.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty plants for pollinators in the Wildlife Garden and trims his box topiary cones. He also takes succulent leaf cuttings and continues the summer veg harvest. Meanwhile, Carol Klein visits stunning Italian-influenced gardens in Gloucestershire.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty shows how to take cuttings from herbs, prune summer raspberries and plant daylilies. Meanwhile, Adam travels to Whitstable on the Kent coast to see how gardeners cope with the wild, wet and windy weather.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: With autumn just around the corner, Adam takes stock of his garden and plans ahead for some late-season interest under the supervision of Ash the cat. Plus, Frances visits a garden in Kent where the plants provide a non-stop buffet for insects.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty plants bulbs in pots, including hyacinths and daffodils. He shares tips and advice on what to do when apples and pears have been affected by diseases such as canker and brown rot. Plus, he gives a timely guide on how to collect and save seeds.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty considers a revamp of his cottage garden, divides perennials to get new plants for free and plants bulbs in pots for spring.

programme.title: Colisión
programme.desc: Una esposa y una amante se enfrentan por el corazón de un hombre. Todo culmina en un enfrentamiento final, y alguien termina muerto.

programme.title: Calor de Miami
programme.desc: Después de matar al hombre al que creía involucrado en un brutal ataque que dejó a su esposo muerto y a su pequeño hijo herido, una mujer afirma que actuó en defensa propia.

programme.title: Indescriptible
programme.desc: La celebración de aniversario de una pareja termina en tragedia cuando uno de ellos es asesinado en lo que parecía ser un allanamiento de morada. Sin embargo, los investigadores creen que el sospechoso tenía vínculos con la víctima.

programme.title: Un triángulo mortal
programme.desc: Tres mejores amigos compartían grandes sueños. Luego, uno de ellos desapareció. ¿Pudo un romance secreto haber llevado a la tragedia?

programme.title: La muerte de Gianni Versace
programme.desc: La pareja de Gianni Versace, Antonio D'Amico, habla sobre el asesinato del ícono de la moda. La muerte de Versace ocurrió durante una persecución que duró varios meses para dar con Andrew Cunanan, acusado de cometer otros cuatro asesinatos en 1997.

programme.title: Relación al descubierto
programme.desc: Roberta descubre la relación que tiene Diego con Paola. Por su lado, Mía se va del colegio y le deja una carta a Celina. En tanto, Miguel, con ayuda de Mayra, sale del colegio para buscarla.

programme.title: Sentimientos encontrados
programme.desc: Giovanni se molesta al enterarse de que Miguel fue a buscar a Mía. Por su parte, Roberta encuentra a Mía con Alma y se siente traicionada. Luego, Alma le dice a Madariaga que Mía está con ella.

programme.title: Amor prohibido
programme.desc: José le dice a Roberta que se supone que ella anda con Teo. Por su lado, Miguel termina con Julieta. Finalmente, Pilar le cuenta a Lupita que está embarazada.

programme.title: Celos entre compañeras
programme.desc: Roberta por celos, le pide a Alma elegir entre Mía y ella. Por su parte, Miguel le dice a Giovanni que Mía no es para él, y luego le confiesa a Mía lo que siente por ella.

programme.title: Decepciones
programme.desc: Franco cree que Alma es quien pone a Mía en su contra. Por su lado, Miguel no quiere seguir ocultando su relación con Mía.

programme.title: Un nuevo amor
programme.desc: Alma llega a casa de Franco y la besa estando borracho. Por su parte, Nico trata de que Miguel asuma que es novio de Mía. Finalmente, Mía le confiesa a Giovanni que está enamorada de otro y termina con él.

programme.title: Sobre aviso
programme.desc: Los chicos salen a la discoteca y tratan de ligar con unas chavas de la escuela religiosa. Por su parte, Mía no quiere tener relaciones con Miguel.

programme.title: Fuera de la banda
programme.desc: La banda toca en un café. Por su parte, Diego se reconcilia con Paola. Además, Mía quiere saber de su madre e intenta saber la verdad.

programme.title: Chismes
programme.desc: León le dice a Alma que Roberta y Diego pasaron la noche juntos. Por su parte, Giovanni sustituye a Diego y participa en la carrera de jinetes. Además, Pilar se hace la prueba de embarazo.

programme.title: Cubriendo apariencias
programme.desc: Mía y su papá se encuentran a Alma en la playa, Roberta cubre a Diego en un problema con su papá. Por su parte, León se enfurece al descubrir que Giovanni usurpó el lugar de Diego.

programme.title: Atrapado
programme.desc: Alma tiene una discusión con Franco y lo avienta al mar por insinuar que es una mujer interesada. Diego es atrapado por los hombres de la logia.

programme.title: Cantando con el alma
programme.desc: Diego, Giovanni, Roberta, Lupita, Miguel y Mía tienen éxito en su show. Además, Mabel y Diego se encuentran en el café. Giovanni se avergüenza de su mamá cuando la mamá de Tomás la invita a su casa.

programme.title: El hijo verdadero
programme.desc: Luisa se entera de que Giovanni se avergüenza de ella, ya que intenta hacerle creer a Tomás que ella no es su madre, pues no quiere que descubra la verdad. Luisa le dice a Nora que Giovanni no es su verdadero hijo.

programme.title: Secreto importante
programme.desc: Lupita descubre que Nico sabe por qué Miguel actúa tan raro con Mía y trata de convencerlo de contarle la verdad. Mía le dice a Miguel que a veces siente que no la quiere por la forma en que la trata.

programme.title: Venganza
programme.desc: Carlo le dice a Franco que quiere volver a trabajar en la empresa. Lupita descubre que Miguel quiere vengarse de la familia de Mía y trata de descubrir por qué.

programme.title: Otra relación
programme.desc: Lupita sigue a Miguel y lo encuentra besando a otra mujer. Miguel le confiesa a Julieta que está enamorado de Mía y decide terminar su relación con ella.

programme.title: Triste confesión
programme.desc: Lupita le dice a Mía que Miguel es su novio por una venganza. Como respuesta, Mía insulta a Miguel y les dice a todos que estuvo con él por una apuesta. Mientras tanto, Teo es nombrado por la logia como cuidador de cuarto.

programme.title: Engaño de una hija
programme.desc: Roberta no quiere que la fama de su mamá opaque su carrera en la banda. Mientras tanto, Mía abofetea a Miguel. Sin piedad, Esteban se excede en sus castigos hacia los alumnos.

programme.title: Verdaderas intenciones
programme.desc: Carlo le dice a Roberta que está interesado en su mamá y no en ella. Además, el Sr. Mendiola despide a Esteban y presenta a Gastón como el nuevo prefecto. Por su parte, José le confiesa a Teo que fue ella quien le escribía los mails y no Roberta.

programme.title: El disco
programme.desc: Mía abandona la banda y a Miguel le da gusto, pero Diego le dice que sería un error. Por su parte, El Oso logra que Marcelino se vaya con él. La banda va a su entrevista con la disquera.

programme.title: La oveja negra
programme.desc: Los chicos de la banda necesitan ser invitados al programa Otro Rollo para darse a conocer. Celina y José planean reencontrar a la maestra Hilda con su amor del pasado, para salvarse del examen. Franco le da otra oportunidad a Carlos para trabajar.

programme.title: Encubridores
programme.desc: Tomás y Giovanni tratan de encubrir a Diego con Alicia. Por su parte, Madariaga se molesta con Gandía por contratar a una profesora solo por ser recomendada. Además, Rosa se quiere llevar a Lupita del colegio.

programme.title: La indiscreta
programme.desc: Celina cae en la trampa de Gandía y delata a Roberta. Mabel encubre a los chicos y le dice a Gandía que ella autorizó su salida. Celina decide irse del colegio. Roberta le pide perdón a Teo. José culpa a Lupita de escribir los anónimos sobre Teo.

programme.title: Nace RBD
programme.desc: Mayra intenta que Lupita no se vaya con Rosa a Guadalajara. Mía, Giovanni, Miguel, Lupita, Diego y Roberta deciden que su banda se llame RBD.

programme.title: Presentación en televisión
programme.desc: Adal Ramones escucha cantar a los chicos y los deja cantar en su programa. Celina, Vico, José, Nico y Tomás deben lograr que nadie vea el programa. RBD canta en el programa Otro Rollo. La policía le dice a Alma que encontraron el cadáver de un niño.

programme.title: Amigos
programme.desc: Celina y Vico le cuentan a Mía lo que hicieron para que nadie los viera en televisión. Por otro lado, la cita de Hilda y su antiguo enamorado sale mal.

programme.title: La búsqueda
programme.desc: Alma pide ayuda en televisión para a encontrar a Marcelino. Lupita le dice a Madariaga que Roberta y Jose cometieron un error al pensar que el Sr. Calderón era el enamorado de Hilda.

programme.title: Tranquilidad
programme.desc: Franco le ofrece su ayuda a Alma. Roberta besa a Diego. Paola le exige a Diego dejar su banda para que no esté cerca de Roberta. Nico le pide a Lupita que piense en su futuro y no deje el colegio. Marcelino llama a Roberta para despedirse.

programme.title: Peligro de separación
programme.desc: Diego decide dejar la banda, pero Nico le dice que tiene un contrato firmado. Por su parte, Rosa lleva a Dulce al colegio para chantajear a Lupita.

programme.title: El enamorado
programme.desc: Mía inicia una campaña para ayudar a la conservación del Bosque de Chapultepec. Por su parte, Mayra felicita a Lupita por decidir quedarse en el colegio.

programme.title: Rumores
programme.desc: Diego le confiesa a su mamá que la mujer que ama es Paola. Pascual no quiere que Galia trabaje en el colegio. Gastón amenaza a José. Roberta le pide a Facundo que no acepte a Diego en su banda. León recibe un correo con fotos de Diego y Paola.

programme.title: La nueva maestra
programme.desc: Roberta se enoja al saber que Alma es la maestra de coreografía. Por su parte, Mía se enoja con Miguel por inventar que sale con Gastón.

programme.title: Oscuras intenciones
programme.desc: León amenaza a Paula y le da la oportunidad de terminar con Diego sin que sepa la verdad. Por su parte, la logia obliga a Teo a robarse la cartera de la profesora Renata.

programme.title: La modelo
programme.desc: Roberta ayuda a Diego a escapar del colegio. Por su parte, Gandía le pide a José devolver lo que robó, para no expulsarla. Además, Paola le dice a Diego que quiere una vida nueva en donde nadie la conozca.

programme.title: Escapando juntos
programme.desc: Diego se escapa con Paula y Roberta trata de impedirlo. Por su parte, Franco soborna a Alma para que se aleje de su familia. Mientras tanto, Roberta le dice a Paola que revele qué relación tenía con León.

programme.title: Robos misteriosos
programme.desc: Alma utiliza el dinero que le dio Franco para donarlo a una casa hogar para niños con cáncer a nombre de él. En tanto, los profesores son robados y sus pertenencias aparecen en el escritorio del director.

programme.title: Romance prohibido
programme.desc: José conoce a su tutor. Por su parte, los de la Logia están furiosos porque no lograron que José fuera expulsado. Además, Nico le dice a Teo que fue muy arriesgado su plan para ayudar a José.

programme.title: Modelo al descubierto
programme.desc: Roberta planea un viaje para que Mabel busque a Diego en Puebla. Por su parte, Franco descubre que Mía es modelo de una campaña de lencería. Además, Alma es amenazada por Coluchi.

programme.title: Ilusiones
programme.desc: Mía cree que olvidará a Miguel. Por su lado, Teo le dice a Miguel y Nico lo que pasó con el cuidador, y sospechan de Tomás y Giovanni.

programme.title: Extraña relación
programme.desc: León le dice a Mabel que Paola es prostituta. Mabel le pide a Roberta que le haga creer a León que Diego se fugó con ella.

programme.title: Otro tipo de mujer
programme.desc: Paola, en el Hospital, rechaza a Diego cuando ve que llega León. Por su parte, Nico le prohíbe a Tomás salir con Lupita. León le dice a Diego que Paola es una prostituta.

programme.title: Padres contratados
programme.desc: Pilar aconseja a Lupita; Gastón invita a Mía; Franco y Valeria van al colegio; creen que Mía los rechazó por Gastón; Giovanni contrata a unos actores para que sean sus papás.

programme.title: La decisión de Celina
programme.desc: Raquel descubre a los actores. Por su parte, León ve triste a Diego y le dice que el hombre debe dominar y se abrazan. Mientras tanto, Franco se entera de que Carlo fue preso por carreras clandestinas.

programme.title: Cubriendo espaldas
programme.desc: Celina desea ser monja por Augusto. Por su lado, Paola busca a Diego para volver. Mientras tanto, Damiana hace una cena para Celina y Francisco. Además, Diego perdona a Paola y no regresan.

programme.title: Sinceridad
programme.desc: Nico termina su noviazgo con Karen. Para herir a Roberta, Paola le dice que se reconcilió con Diego. Por su parte, Teo es aceptado en la Logia.

programme.title: En peligro
programme.desc: Lupita habla con Pilar y le dice que se la pasa bien con Tomás, pero con el solo escuchar el nombre de Nico, todo se le olvida. El padre de Diego le regala un auto lo cual le molesta, porque solo trata de comprar su cariño.

programme.title: Captura y tortura
programme.desc: Valeria le propone a Franco vivir juntos, él le dice que lo ha pensado, pero no puede porque Mía es su prioridad y debe estar libre para ella. Debido a la ruptura de Nico y Karen, el padre de ella le prohíbe ir al café y olvidarse de la banda.

programme.title: La pelea
programme.desc: La banda se entera de que Gastón estuvo en el café y los vio tocar. Galia habla con Pilar y le dice que cada una deberá enfrentar sus errores. Mía pelea con Miguel por culpa de Luz Viviana, ella amenaza con contarle a su papá que está en la banda.

programme.title: En riesgo
programme.desc: Giovanni logra escapar de La Logia, Miguel y los demás chicos denuncian con el director que Giovanni y Teo no están en el colegio. Tomás y Lupita están discutiendo y escuchan un golpe.

programme.title: El traidor
programme.desc: Afortunadamente, Teo no está muerto, Enrique y los chicos lo reaniman mientras esperan a los paramédicos. Carlo le dice a Alma que alguien debe poner a Roberta en su lugar. Pascual no cree sobre la existencia de La Logia.

programme.title: Los secretos de la Logia
programme.desc: José visita a Teo en el hospital y le dice que lo ama. Alma toma la decisión de irse debido al comportamiento de Roberta. Giovanni les confiesa que sabe dónde están los archivos de La Logia.

programme.title: Consecuencias
programme.desc: La habitación de la azotea arde en llamas, Pascual y Galia corren para controlar el fuego, sin saber que Diego y los demás alumnos. El director Pascual y Mendiola no saben qué hacer con los alumnos que forman La Logia.
